hints: Look at the mole ratios in the balanced equation, one mole of carbonate does not make one mole of everything.
Start with 0.025 mol of sodium carbonate and use the 1:2:2:1 ratio to find moles of HCl needed, NaCl made and CO2 made.
Convert those moles into volume with V = n/c, gas volume with 24000 cm3 per mole at RTP, and mass with m = n x Mr to check each statement.
walkthrough:
**Find the reacting moles from the equation**

Think of the equation as a recipe. One mole of carbonate needs two moles of acid and makes two moles of salt and one mole of gas.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Check statement 1 for carbon dioxide volume**

Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ = moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ = 0.025 mol because the ratio is 1:1.

At room temperature and pressure, 1 mol of gas = $24000 \text{ cm}^3$:
$$V = 0.025 \times 24000 = 600 \text{ cm}^3$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 for acid volume**

Moles of $\text{HCl}$ needed = $2 \times 0.025 = 0.050$ mol because the ratio is 1:2.

Use $V = n / c$:
$$V = \frac{0.050}{0.2} = 0.25 \text{ dm}^3 = 250 \text{ cm}^3$$
So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 for salt mass**

Moles of $\text{NaCl}$ made = $2 \times 0.025 = 0.050$ mol because the ratio is 1:2.

$M_r$ of $\text{NaCl} = 23.0 + 35.5 = 58.5$. Use $m = n \times M_r$:
$$m = 0.050 \times 58.5 = 2.925 \text{ g}$$
This is double 1.46 g, so statement 3 is incorrect. Statements 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims all three statements are true. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 gives half the correct mass. 0.05 mol of NaCl has mass 2.93 g, not 1.46 g.
options.B: Correct because only statements 1 and 2 are true. 0.025 mol CO2 is 600 cm3 at RTP, and 0.05 mol HCl at 0.2 mol dm-3 is 250 cm3. Statement 3 is false as the true mass is about 2.93 g.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. Statement 3 forgets the 1:2 ratio for NaCl. Many students use 0.025 mol instead of 0.05 mol and get 1.46 g.
options.D: Incorrect because it leaves out statement 2. Statement 2 is correct when you apply n = c x V properly. 0.05 mol divided by 0.2 mol dm-3 really is 0.25 dm3.
